title: Stimulus calibration changes link-location certificates in two passive adult worm models
abstract: We tested one-link location with uncertain change size in passive models of two partial adult worm maps. Each model had 180 cells. A link conductance increased by 0.5 to 2 times its baseline weight. We compared finite response segments under an assumed total measurement error. With 20 observed cells and current scaled to keep isolated-cell voltage fixed, the lowest tested leak certified mean shares of 0 and 0.011 percent of links. A fixed-current control certified 70.59 and 69.28 percent at that leak. At primary leak both tests gave 8.42 and 8.18 percent. Unit response signatures retained large separation at low leak but used a different error model. The scaled-current response tends to zero at both leak limits. Thus stimulus calibration limits the interpretation of a low-leak signature benefit. Error levels, conductance and stimulus ranges were assumed, not measured. Incomplete electrical maps, known baselines and no activity data limit biological use. Code, aggregate evidence, figures, hashes and retrieval steps support reproduction. External records are not bundled.

display.caption: Stimulus calibration changes the link identity certificate. Fixed-current control was exploratory. The normalized-signature curve uses a different error model.
Partial panel certificates under fixed isolated-cell voltage stimulation. Bands show design variation, not animal uncertainty.
